messages:
alex_csm: Fwd from customer: getting "limit exceeded" on rerank, but they say doc list is small. billing spike too. Can someone triage? jane.k: Can you paste the exact API request/response they saw? alex_csm: Sure, here's the core of the payload (sanitized): alex_csm: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \\n -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx' \\n -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n -d '{"query": "
Hello, this is my question...","documents":[{"id":"1","text":"

Very long HTML doc with lots of tags & entities...

"},{"id":"2","text":"

Another doc with escaped\"quotes\" and many   entities

"}]}'``` jane.k: Response? alex_csm: They got 413-like message in UI: "input size limit exceeded" plus meter spike shows +200k tokens billed in one call. matt.s: Hmm, HTML entities and backslash-escaped quotes can expand tokens. Do they send pre-escaped JSON string from client? The example shows double-escaped sequences. leo.dev: I pulled the raw request from logs for that app id. The client is embedding pre-escaped HTML inside a JSON string, and then a frontend layer escapes again. Effective payload includes lots of literal `\\u00a0` and `\u003c` sequences which the tokenizer treats as separate tokens. jane.k: That would explain token inflation. Any repro I can paste to customer? matt.s: Quick repro we used: matt.s: ```bash PAYLOAD='{"query":"

Q

","documents":[{"id":"1","text":"'"'

'"'"A long text with   and lots of > < sequences'"'"'}]}' curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$PAYLOAD" -w "\\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\n" ``` matt.s: With the double-escaped payload we measured ~60k token-equivalent vs <2k when sending cleaned text. alex_csm: Customer asks: is this a bug in your token counting or their client? leo.dev: It's both: our tokenizer counts whatever bytes arrive after JSON decoding. If the app double-escapes, the decoded string contains literal backslashes and unicode escapes which explode tokenization. We should show clearer guidance and give a friendly error with a hint: "looks like escaped HTML or JSON; try sending raw text or decode client-side". jane.k: For immediate triage to customer: 1) confirm if they double-escape on client, 2) suggest sending stripped text (strip tags) or decode JSON before sending, 3) recommend limiting docs per request with page-based reranking. alex_csm: I put together a short repro guide for the customer with a safe curl that demonstrates the difference. Want it in the reply? matt.s: Please. Also include a small Node snippet to decode vs not decode so they can see token counts. alex_csm: Replying to customer now with repro, mitigation steps, and note we flagged for UX improvement (error hint). Will follow up if they're still seeing billing spikes. :thumbsup: sre-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2026-934 "Rerank token-inflation by escaped HTML". Assigned to eng-runtime for UX follow-up. leo.dev: Filed a short internal issue with repro and suggested error copy: "Input appears to contain escaped HTML/JSON sequences; consider sending decoded/plain text to avoid unexpectedly large token counts." jane.k: Thanks team. If they send a sample full request we can run a one-off tokenization analysis and return a token breakdown per doc. alex_csm: Customer acknowledged, will send sample tomorrow. Closing for now but keeping it monitored.
